drills.sentence: 自転車で通学すれば運動にもなるし交通費も浮くので、まさに（　　）だ。
drills.en: Commuting by bike gives you exercise and saves the fare, so it really kills two birds with one stone.
drills.explanation: 一石二鳥 = one action brings two benefits (exercise + saving money).

drills.sentence: 好きな給食のメニューは（　　）で、クラスでアンケートをとっても意見がばらばらだった。
drills.en: Everyone has a different favourite school lunch; when the class did a survey the answers were all over the place.
drills.explanation: 十人十色 = ten people, ten colours: tastes differ from person to person. 異口同音 would mean everyone said the same thing.

drills.sentence: 先生が「遠足は中止です」と言うと、みんなは（　　）に「えーっ」と声を上げた。
drills.en: When the teacher said the field trip was cancelled, everyone cried "Nooo!" in unison.
drills.explanation: 異口同音 = many mouths, the same sound: everyone saying the same thing at once, usually as 異口同音に.

drills.sentence: 弟は「明日は大雪になる」という天気予報を（　　）で聞いていた。
drills.en: My little brother listened to the forecast of heavy snow tomorrow half believing it.
drills.explanation: 半信半疑 = half believing, half doubting.

drills.sentence: 試合の最後の数分間は（　　）で走ったので、何も覚えていない。
drills.en: I ran completely absorbed for the last few minutes of the match, so I don't remember anything.
drills.explanation: 無我夢中 = so absorbed that you forget yourself.

drills.sentence: 前半で三点リードしていても（　　）だから、最後まで気を抜くな。
drills.en: Even with a three-point lead at half time, carelessness is your worst enemy, so stay focused to the end.
drills.explanation: 油断大敵 = carelessness is a great enemy; a warning not to relax too early.

drills.sentence: 九回裏、四番打者の（　　）のホームランで、チームは逆転勝ちした。
drills.en: In the bottom of the ninth, the cleanup hitter's game-saving home run turned the game around for the team.
drills.explanation: 起死回生 = bringing the dying back to life: a move that rescues a hopeless situation.

drills.sentence: 道に迷ったうえに雨まで降ってきて、ぼくたちは（　　）のピンチだった。
drills.en: We were lost and then it started raining too: we were in a desperate fix.
drills.explanation: 絶体絶命のピンチ is the set phrase for a situation with no way out.

drills.sentence: 火災報知器が鳴ったとき、出口がわからず、みんなは（　　）した。
drills.en: When the fire alarm went off, nobody knew where the exit was and everyone ran around in confusion.
drills.explanation: 右往左往 = moving this way and that in confusion. 東奔西走 is running around busily for a purpose.

drills.sentence: 何度も（　　）を重ねて、ようやく紙飛行機が遠くまで飛ぶようになった。
drills.en: After lots of trial and error, the paper plane finally started flying a long way.
drills.explanation: 試行錯誤を重ねる = to go through repeated trial and error.

drills.sentence: 漢字の力は（　　）には身につかない。毎日少しずつ練習しよう。
drills.en: Kanji skills are not acquired overnight. Let's practise a little every day.
drills.explanation: 一朝一夕には〜ない = cannot be done in a short time.

drills.sentence: 新学期から（　　）、毎朝六時に起きることにした。
drills.en: With the new term I made a fresh start and decided to get up at six every morning.
drills.explanation: 心機一転 = changing your mindset and starting afresh.

drills.sentence: 横断歩道で自転車とぶつかりそうになったが、（　　）のところでよけた。
drills.en: I nearly collided with a bicycle at the crossing but dodged it by a hair's breadth.
drills.explanation: 危機一髪 = danger hanging by a single hair; a very narrow escape.

drills.sentence: 雨で運動会の予定が変わったが、先生たちは（　　）に対応してくれた。
drills.en: The sports day schedule changed because of the rain, but the teachers adapted flexibly.
drills.explanation: 臨機応変に対応する = to respond flexibly to the situation.

drills.sentence: 姉は（　　）で、レストランのメニューを決めるのにいつも十分以上かかる。
drills.en: My big sister is so indecisive that it always takes her more than ten minutes to choose from a restaurant menu.
drills.explanation: 優柔不断 = unable to make up your mind.

drills.sentence: 夜ふかしして朝寝坊したのは（　　）だから、文句を言ってもしかたがない。
drills.en: You overslept because you stayed up late; you brought it on yourself, so there's no point complaining.
drills.explanation: 自業自得 = suffering the results of your own actions.

drills.sentence: 長年の友だちなので、目を見ただけで（　　）で気持ちが通じる。
drills.en: We have been friends for years, so we understand each other's feelings just by looking at each other.
drills.explanation: 以心伝心 = understanding passes from heart to heart without words.

drills.sentence: 旅先で出会った人との（　　）を大切にしたい。
drills.en: I want to treasure each once-in-a-lifetime meeting with people I meet on my travels.
drills.explanation: 一期一会 = every encounter may happen only once, so treasure it.

drills.sentence: 健康のために始めたジョギングで無理をしてけがをするのは（　　）だ。
drills.en: Pushing too hard and getting hurt jogging, which you started for your health, is putting the cart before the horse.
drills.explanation: 本末転倒 = confusing the essential with the incidental.

drills.sentence: 初めて一人でカレーを作ったときは、玉ねぎを切るのに（　　）した。
drills.en: The first time I made curry by myself, I struggled terribly just cutting the onions.
drills.explanation: 四苦八苦する = to have a very hard time with something.

drills.sentence: テストの点数に（　　）せず、まちがえたところを見直そう。
drills.en: Don't swing between joy and worry over every test score; go back over the mistakes instead.
drills.explanation: 一喜一憂する = to be happy one moment and worried the next as things change.

drills.sentence: 弟は自分で描いた絵を「天才的だ」と（　　）している。
drills.en: My little brother is praising his own drawing, calling it a work of genius.
drills.explanation: 自画自賛 = praising your own picture: blowing your own trumpet.

drills.sentence: 校長先生がプールに飛びこむなんて、（　　）の出来事だ。
drills.en: The principal jumping into the pool? That's unheard of!
drills.explanation: 前代未聞 = never heard of in any previous age.

drills.sentence: 事故を目撃した女の子は、その（　　）を警察官に話した。
drills.en: The girl who witnessed the accident told the police officer the whole story from start to finish.
drills.explanation: 一部始終 = the whole thing from beginning to end.

drills.sentence: 姉は（　　）な性格で、遠足の前日には雨具もばんそうこうも準備している。
drills.en: My sister is so well-prepared that the day before a trip she already has her rain gear and plasters ready.
drills.explanation: 用意周到 = thoroughly prepared.

drills.sentence: 母が何度注意しても、兄にとっては（　　）で、少しも聞いていない。
drills.en: No matter how often Mum tells him off, it goes in one ear and out the other with my brother.
drills.explanation: 馬耳東風 = like the east wind in a horse's ear: advice that is ignored.

drills.sentence: 科学技術は（　　）で、数年前のスマートフォンがもう古く感じる。
drills.en: Technology advances so rapidly that a smartphone from a few years ago already feels old.
drills.explanation: 日進月歩 = progressing day by day, month by month.

drills.sentence: 祖父は五十歳を過ぎてから画家として認められた。まさに（　　）だ。
drills.en: My grandfather was only recognised as a painter after he turned fifty. A true late bloomer.
drills.explanation: 大器晩成 = great talents mature late.

drills.sentence: 力持ちの田中くんに荷物運びを任せるなんて、（　　）だね。
drills.en: Giving the heavy lifting to strong Tanaka: that's the right person in the right place.
drills.explanation: 適材適所 = assigning each person to the job that suits them.

drills.sentence: 調べた情報が多すぎるので、（　　）して大事なものだけを発表に使おう。
drills.en: We found too much information, so let's sort it and use only the important parts in the presentation.
drills.explanation: 取捨選択 = choosing what to keep and what to discard.

drills.sentence: 前置きはいいから、（　　）に言ってほしい。
drills.en: Skip the preamble and just tell me straight.
drills.explanation: 単刀直入に言う = to get straight to the point.

drills.sentence: 転校生の山本さんとはゲームの話で（　　）し、すぐに親友になった。
drills.en: I hit it off with Yamamoto, the new transfer student, talking about games, and we soon became best friends.
drills.explanation: 意気投合する = to hit it off, to find you are of one mind.

drills.sentence: 妹は（　　）がはっきりしていて、気持ちがすぐ顔に出る。
drills.en: My little sister shows her emotions clearly; her feelings appear on her face right away.
drills.explanation: 喜怒哀楽 = joy, anger, sorrow and pleasure: the full range of emotions.

drills.sentence: 作文は（　　）を意識して書くと、読みやすくなる。
drills.en: If you keep introduction, development, twist and conclusion in mind, your composition will be easier to read.
drills.explanation: 起承転結 = the classic four-part structure of a text.

drills.sentence: 「毎日百回なわとびをする」と宣言した兄は、その言葉どおり（　　）した。
drills.en: My brother announced he would jump rope a hundred times every day, and he did exactly as he said.
drills.explanation: 有言実行 = saying what you will do and then doing it.

drills.sentence: 最初は張り切っていた日記も三日で終わり、（　　）になってしまった。
drills.en: I was so keen on my diary at first, but it stopped after three days: a great start that fizzled out.
drills.explanation: 竜頭蛇尾 = a dragon's head and a snake's tail: a strong start and a weak finish.

drills.sentence: 祖母の病状は（　　）で、なかなか良くならない。
drills.en: Grandma's condition goes back and forth and isn't getting much better.
drills.explanation: 一進一退 = one step forward, one step back.

drills.sentence: だれにでもいい顔をする（　　）は、かえって信用されないこともある。
drills.en: Someone who tries to please everybody may actually end up not being trusted.
drills.explanation: 八方美人 = beautiful from all eight directions: a people-pleaser (slightly negative).

drills.sentence: 昔の遊びを調べて新しいゲームを考えるのは、まさに（　　）だ。
drills.en: Researching old games to invent a new one is exactly learning the new from the old.
drills.explanation: 温故知新 = gaining new insight by studying the past.

drills.sentence: 町内会長の祖父は（　　）ので、商店街の人はみんな知り合いだ。
drills.en: My grandfather, head of the neighbourhood association, knows lots of people, so he's acquainted with everyone on the shopping street.
drills.explanation: 顔が広い = to have a wide circle of acquaintances.

drills.sentence: 年末のケーキ屋さんは（　　）ほど忙しい。
drills.en: At the end of the year the cake shop is so busy they'd take help from anyone.
drills.explanation: 猫の手も借りたい = so busy you would even borrow a cat's paws.

drills.sentence: 弟のいたずらには、両親もすっかり（　　）いる。
drills.en: Even my parents are at their wits' end with my little brother's pranks.
drills.explanation: 手を焼く = to have a hard time dealing with someone.

drills.sentence: 「整理整頓ができていない」という先生の話は、ぼくにとって（　　）話だった。
drills.en: The teacher's talk about untidy desks struck a painful chord with me.
drills.explanation: 耳が痛い = criticism that hits home.

drills.sentence: 彼女は（　　）から、秘密を打ち明けても大丈夫だ。
drills.en: She can keep a secret, so it's safe to confide in her.
drills.explanation: 口が堅い = tight-lipped. 口が軽い is the opposite.

drills.sentence: 息子が作文コンクールで入賞して、母は（　　）。
drills.en: Her son won a prize in the essay contest, and his mother is very proud.
drills.explanation: 鼻が高い = proud (of yourself or of family).

drills.sentence: 祖父母は、孫が遊びに来るのを（　　）待っている。
drills.en: The grandparents are eagerly waiting for their grandchild to visit.
drills.explanation: 首を長くして待つ = to wait eagerly.

drills.sentence: 小学生とは思えないピアノの腕前に、大人たちも（　　）。
drills.en: The adults were amazed at the child's piano skills, far beyond an elementary schooler's.
drills.explanation: 舌を巻く = to be deeply impressed.

drills.sentence: 一回戦で負けて、選手たちは（　　）帰っていった。
drills.en: After losing in the first round, the players went home with drooping shoulders.
drills.explanation: 肩を落とす = to be discouraged, disappointed.

drills.sentence: 手品で消えたコインがポケットから出てきて、妹は（　　）。
drills.en: The coin that vanished in the magic trick came out of my sister's pocket, and her eyes went wide.
drills.explanation: 目を丸くする = to be wide-eyed with surprise.

drills.sentence: 性格は正反対だが、あの二人はなぜか（　　）らしい。
drills.en: Their personalities are complete opposites, yet somehow those two get along well.
drills.explanation: 馬が合う = to hit it off with someone.

drills.sentence: テストが終わったので、週末は温泉で（　　）つもりだ。
drills.en: The exams are over, so this weekend I plan to relax at a hot spring.
drills.explanation: 羽を伸ばす = to stretch your wings: to relax freely.

drills.sentence: おつかいの途中で（　　）いないで、早く帰ってきなさい。
drills.en: Don't dawdle on your errand; come straight home.
drills.explanation: 油を売る = to idle away time when you should be working.

drills.sentence: けんかのことはもう（　　）、また一緒に遊ぼう。
drills.en: Let's forget about the fight and play together again.
drills.explanation: 水に流す = to let bygones be bygones.

drills.sentence: 相手は全国大会の優勝チームで、ぼくたちはまったく（　　）。
drills.en: Our opponents were the national champions, and we were no match for them at all.
drills.explanation: 歯が立たない = to be no match for someone.

drills.sentence: 提出する前に、もう一度作文に（　　）ください。
drills.en: Please look over your composition once more before handing it in.
drills.explanation: 目を通す = to look over, to skim through a text.

drills.sentence: リーダーは、みんなの意見に（　　）ことが大切だ。
drills.en: It's important for a leader to listen carefully to everyone's opinions.
drills.explanation: 耳を傾ける = to listen attentively.

drills.sentence: 大人が話しているときに、横から（　　）のはやめなさい。
drills.en: Stop butting in while the adults are talking.
drills.explanation: 口を挟む = to interrupt, to cut into a conversation.

drills.sentence: クラスのみんなは、何でも知っている佐藤さんに（　　）いる。
drills.en: Everyone in the class looks up to Sato, who knows everything.
drills.explanation: 一目置く = to acknowledge someone as superior (from go handicaps).

drills.sentence: 何度教えても覚えないので、とうとうコーチも（　　）しまった。
drills.en: He never remembered no matter how often he was taught, so in the end even the coach gave up on him.
drills.explanation: さじを投げる = to throw away the spoon: to give up as hopeless.

drills.sentence: 母は「ゲームは一時間まで」と兄に（　　）。
drills.en: Mum warned my brother firmly: games for one hour at most.
drills.explanation: 釘を刺す = to give a firm reminder in advance.

drills.sentence: 算数が得意な兄が計算まちがいをするなんて、（　　）だね。
drills.en: My brother, who's great at maths, made a calculation error? Even monkeys fall from trees.
drills.explanation: 猿も木から落ちる = even experts make mistakes.

drills.sentence: 近道の山道は危ないから、（　　）で大通りを行こう。
drills.en: The mountain shortcut is dangerous, so let's take the main road: more haste, less speed.
drills.explanation: 急がば回れ = if you're in a hurry, take the long way round.

drills.sentence: （　　）というから、ピアノの練習をもう少し続けてみよう。
drills.en: They say perseverance pays off, so I'll keep practising the piano a bit longer.
drills.explanation: 石の上にも三年 = even a cold stone warms if you sit on it for three years.

drills.sentence: お花見に来たのに、弟は桜も見ないで食べてばかり。まさに（　　）だ。
drills.en: We came to see the cherry blossoms, but my brother just eats without looking at them. Dumplings over flowers indeed.
drills.explanation: 花より団子 = preferring practical things (food) over beauty.

drills.sentence: さがしていためがねが自分の頭の上にあったなんて、（　　）だ。
drills.en: The glasses I was looking for were on my own head. It's darkest under the lamp.
drills.explanation: 灯台下暗し = what is closest is hardest to see.

drills.sentence: 財布を落としたうえに雨にぬれて、（　　）だった。
drills.en: I lost my wallet and then got soaked in the rain: misfortunes never come singly.
drills.explanation: 泣きっ面に蜂 = a bee sting on a crying face: one bad thing after another.

drills.sentence: （　　）というように、実際に工場を見学して多くのことがわかった。
drills.en: As they say, seeing is believing: visiting the factory in person taught us a lot.
drills.explanation: 百聞は一見に如かず = seeing once beats hearing a hundred times.

drills.sentence: （　　）だから、家族で防災リュックを用意しておこう。
drills.en: If you're prepared, you needn't worry, so let's get the family's emergency backpacks ready.
drills.explanation: 備えあれば憂いなし = being prepared removes worry.

drills.sentence: 明日から夏休みなので、（　　）してなかなか眠れない。
drills.en: Summer vacation starts tomorrow, so I'm too excited to sleep.
drills.explanation: わくわく = excited anticipation.

drills.sentence: 遠足で疲れたので、その夜は（　　）眠った。
drills.en: I was tired from the field trip, so I slept soundly that night.
drills.explanation: ぐっすり眠る = to sleep soundly.
手本 and 模範 both mean a model or example to follow.
短所 (weak point) ≈ 欠点 (fault). 長所 is the antonym.
長所 (strong point) ≈ 美点 (good point, merit).
方法 (method) ≈ 手段 (means). 目的 is the goal the means serves.
準備 and 用意 both mean preparation.
役割 and 役目 both mean one's role or duty.
経験 (experience) ≈ 体験 (personal, first-hand experience).
独特 and 特有 both mean peculiar to, characteristic of.
我慢 and 辛抱 both mean putting up with, enduring.
返事 and 返答 both mean a reply.
賛成 (agreement) ≈ 賛同 (endorsement). 反対 is the antonym.
承知 and 了解 both mean understanding and accepting.
関心 (concern, interest) ≈ 興味 (interest). Careful: 感心 means admiration.
永遠 and 永久 both mean eternity, permanence.
誠意 (sincerity) ≈ 真心 (true heart, sincerity).
節約 and 倹約 both mean saving, economising. 浪費 (waste) is the opposite.
意外 and 案外 both mean unexpected, contrary to expectation.
不意 and 突然 both mean suddenly, without warning.
誤解 (misunderstanding) ≈ 勘違い (mistaken idea).
解決 (solution) ≈ 決着 (settlement, conclusion of a matter).
故郷 and 郷里 both mean one's hometown.
批判 (criticism) ≈ 非難 (blame, criticism). 賞賛 means praise.
裕福 (wealthy) ≈ 豊か (rich, abundant).
温和 and 穏やか both mean gentle, mild.
心配 (worry) ≈ 不安 (anxiety).
簡単 and 容易 both mean easy.
大雑把 and 大まか both mean rough, not detailed. 几帳面 is the opposite.
徐々に and 次第に both mean gradually.
根拠 (grounds, basis) is close to 理由 (reason).
把握 (grasping a situation) ≈ 理解 (understanding).
懸念 (concern, apprehension) ≈ 心配 (worry).
配慮 (consideration) ≈ 気配り (attentiveness to others).
貴重 (precious) ≈ 大切 (important, precious).
真剣 and 本気 both mean serious, in earnest.
早速 (at once) ≈ すぐ (immediately).
見事 (splendid) ≈ 立派 (fine, admirable).
苦手 and 不得意 both mean being weak at something. 得意 is the antonym.
未来 and 将来 both mean the future.
頑固 and 強情 both mean stubborn. 素直 is the opposite.
陽気 (cheerful) ≈ 快活 (lively, cheerful). 陰気 is the antonym.
楽観的 (optimistic) ↔ 悲観的 (pessimistic).
主観 (subjectivity) ↔ 客観 (objectivity).
具体 (concrete) ↔ 抽象 (abstract).
積極的 (active, positive) ↔ 消極的 (passive, negative).
需要 (demand) ↔ 供給 (supply).
権利 (right) ↔ 義務 (duty).
拡大 (expansion) ↔ 縮小 (reduction).
複雑 (complicated) ↔ 単純 (simple).
理想 (ideal) ↔ 現実 (reality).
増加 (increase) ↔ 減少 (decrease). 縮小 is 'shrink in scale', the opposite of 拡大.
肯定 (affirmation) ↔ 否定 (denial).
集合 (gathering) ↔ 解散 (breaking up, dismissal).
生産 (production) ↔ 消費 (consumption).
輸出 (export) ↔ 輸入 (import).
延長 (extension) ↔ 短縮 (shortening). 縮小 is reduction in size, not in length of time.
平凡 (ordinary) ↔ 非凡 (extraordinary).
勝利 (victory) ↔ 敗北 (defeat).
前進 (moving forward) ↔ 後退 (moving back). 退歩 is the opposite of 進歩 (progress).
天然 (natural) ↔ 人工 (artificial).
束縛 (restraint) ↔ 自由 (freedom).

drills.sentence: 父は地域のボランティア活動をしているので、顔が広い。
drills.explanation: Correct: 顔が広い means knowing many people.

drills.sentence: 姉は顔が広いので、帽子がなかなか合わない。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: 顔が広い is about having many acquaintances, not a physically large face.

drills.sentence: 彼は口が軽いから、大事な秘密は話さないほうがいい。
drills.explanation: Correct: 口が軽い = can't keep secrets.

drills.sentence: 母は口が軽いので、どんな秘密もぜったいにもらさない。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: someone who never leaks secrets is 口が堅い; 口が軽い is the opposite.

drills.sentence: 言うことを聞かない子犬のしつけに手を焼いている。
drills.explanation: Correct: 手を焼く = to have trouble handling something.

drills.sentence: 料理が得意な姉は、毎晩おいしいハンバーグの手を焼いている。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: 手を焼く is not about cooking; it means struggling with someone or something troublesome.

drills.sentence: 妹が県の絵画コンクールで金賞をとって、家族みんな鼻が高い。
drills.explanation: Correct: 鼻が高い = proud.

drills.sentence: テストで0点をとってしまい、鼻が高い思いをした。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: getting zero is shameful; 鼻が高い means proud. 恥ずかしい思い or 顔から火が出る would fit.

drills.sentence: 気が置けない友だちと過ごす時間は、とてもリラックスできる。
drills.explanation: Correct: 気が置けない = so close you need not be on your guard.

drills.sentence: あの人は何を考えているかわからず、気が置けないので油断できない。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: a very common misuse. 気が置けない describes someone you can relax with, not someone untrustworthy.

drills.sentence: 将棋の強い田中さんには、クラスのだれもが一目置いている。
drills.explanation: Correct: 一目置く = to acknowledge someone's superiority.

drills.sentence: 失敗ばかりする弟に、ぼくはいつも一目置いている。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: 一目置く expresses respect, which does not fit someone you consider hopeless.

drills.sentence: 彼は若いころの悪い仲間とは縁を切り、すっかり足を洗った。
drills.explanation: Correct: 足を洗う = to quit a bad way of life.

drills.sentence: 春から新しい部活に足を洗って入部した。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: 足を洗う means quitting something (usually bad), not joining.

drills.sentence: 注文した本が届くのを、首を長くして待っている。
drills.explanation: Correct: 首を長くして待つ = to wait eagerly.

drills.sentence: 宿題がなかなか終わらず、首を長くして困っている。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: 首を長くする is about eager waiting, not being in trouble.

drills.sentence: プロの料理人になるために、毎日腕を磨いている。
drills.explanation: Correct: 腕を磨く = to hone one's skill.

drills.sentence: 転んでけがをしないように、準備運動で腕を磨いた。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: 腕を磨く means improving skill, not warming up your arms.

drills.sentence: 彼のすばらしい演奏に、審査員も舌を巻いた。
drills.explanation: Correct: 舌を巻く = to be amazed and impressed.

drills.sentence: 苦いくすりを飲んで、思わず舌を巻いた。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: 舌を巻く expresses admiration, not a reaction to a bitter taste.

drills.sentence: 昔のけんかは水に流して、仲直りしよう。
drills.explanation: Correct: 水に流す = to forgive and forget.

drills.sentence: 大切な約束を水に流さないように、手帳に書いておいた。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: 水に流す means deliberately forgiving past trouble, not accidentally forgetting something.

drills.sentence: 転校生とは、初めて会った日から馬が合った。
drills.explanation: Correct: 馬が合う = to get along well.

drills.sentence: 休み時間に、校庭で思いきり油を売った。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: 油を売る means slacking off when you should be working; break time is free time anyway.

drills.sentence: 買い物に行った弟が、友だちの家で油を売っていて、なかなか帰ってこない。
drills.explanation: Correct: dawdling on an errand is exactly 油を売る.

drills.sentence: 祖母は甘いものに目がなく、特にようかんが大好きだ。
drills.explanation: Correct: 〜に目がない = to be crazy about something.

drills.sentence: 暗い部屋では目がないので、何も見えない。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: 目がない means having a weakness for something, not being unable to see.

drills.sentence: 「夜ふかしはやめなさい」という医者の言葉は、夜型のぼくには耳が痛かった。
drills.explanation: Correct: advice that hits home is 耳が痛い.

drills.sentence: 学級新聞を完成させるのに、編集係はずいぶん骨を折った。
drills.explanation: Correct: 骨を折る (idiomatic) = to take great pains.

drills.sentence: 弟は親戚の前では猫をかぶって、とてもおとなしくしている。
drills.explanation: Correct: 猫をかぶる = to hide one's true nature and act meek.

drills.sentence: 寒い日は、猫をかぶって暖かくして寝る。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: 猫をかぶる is about pretending to be meek, not keeping warm.

drills.sentence: 値段が高すぎて、買うのに二の足を踏んだ。
drills.explanation: Correct: 二の足を踏む = to hesitate.

drills.sentence: 勢いよく二の足を踏んで、すぐにプールに飛びこんだ。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: 二の足を踏む means hesitating, which contradicts jumping in immediately.

drills.sentence: 窓ふきをしたら部屋がきれいになり、おこづかいももらえた。一石二鳥だ。
drills.explanation: Correct: one action, two benefits.

drills.sentence: 寝坊したうえに忘れ物もして、一石二鳥の失敗だった。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: 一石二鳥 is for gaining two benefits, not suffering two failures.

drills.sentence: 同じ本を読んでも、感想は十人十色だ。
drills.explanation: Correct: impressions differ from person to person.

drills.sentence: 以心伝心なので、友だちに毎日長いメールを送って気持ちを説明している。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: 以心伝心 means understanding without words, so long explanations contradict it.

drills.sentence: 一生懸命練習した結果、優勝できたのは自業自得だ。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: 自業自得 is used for bad results of one's own actions, not for deserved success.

drills.sentence: 注意されても宿題をやらなかったのだから、先生にしかられたのは自業自得だ。
drills.explanation: Correct: being scolded for your own negligence is 自業自得.

drills.sentence: ダイエットのためにジムに通っているのに、帰りに毎回ケーキを食べるのでは本末転倒だ。
drills.explanation: Correct: the action undermines its own purpose.

drills.sentence: 毎朝太陽が東からのぼるのは、前代未聞のことだ。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: 前代未聞 means unprecedented; the sun rising in the east is completely ordinary.

drills.sentence: 妹は一生懸命に逆上がりの練習をしている。
drills.explanation: Correct: 一生懸命 = with all one's might.

drills.sentence: 優柔不断な主将がすぐに作戦を決めてくれたおかげで、試合に勝てた。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: an indecisive captain would not decide quickly.

drills.sentence: 台本どおりにいかなくても、臨機応変に対応すれば大丈夫だ。
drills.explanation: Correct: 臨機応変に = flexibly, according to circumstances.

drills.sentence: 異口同音に反対意見が出て、クラスの意見はまったくまとまらなかった。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: 異口同音 means everyone saying the same thing, so opinions would not be split.

drills.sentence: 泳ぎの苦手な弟がプールでおぼれかけたのは、まさに猿も木から落ちるだ。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: the proverb is about experts making mistakes; the brother is a weak swimmer.

drills.sentence: 料理上手な父がカレーを焦がすなんて、猿も木から落ちるだね。
drills.explanation: Correct: a skilled cook slipping up.

drills.sentence: 慎重な兄は、何事も石橋を叩いて渡るタイプだ。
drills.explanation: Correct: extremely cautious behaviour.

drills.sentence: 夏休みの最後の日に一時間だけ勉強しても、焼け石に水だ。
drills.explanation: Correct: too little effort to make a difference.

drills.sentence: 情けは人の為ならずというから、友だちを甘やかすのはよくない。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: a famous misreading. It means kindness to others eventually comes back to you, not that kindness spoils people.

drills.sentence: 最初はいやだった田舎の生活も、住めば都で、今では大好きだ。
drills.explanation: Correct: any place becomes home once you live there.

drills.sentence: 大好きなおばあちゃんが入院したと聞いて、心配でわくわくした。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: わくわく is joyful excitement; worry would be はらはら or どきどき.

drills.sentence: 夕立で雨がしとしと激しく降り、道路が川のようになった。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: しとしと is quiet, gentle rain; heavy rain is ざあざあ.

drills.sentence: 留学していた姉は、英語がぺらぺらだ。
drills.explanation: Correct: ぺらぺら = fluent.

drills.sentence: 終わったことをいつまでもくよくよしても、しかたがない。
drills.explanation: Correct: くよくよ = brooding over things.

drills.sentence: 彼はてきぱきしているので、何をするにも人の倍の時間がかかる。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: てきぱき means brisk and efficient, the opposite of being slow.

drills.sentence: 春の日差しがぽかぽかと暖かい。
drills.explanation: Correct: ぽかぽか = pleasantly warm.

drills.sentence: 楽しみにしていた花火大会が中止になって、がっかりした。
drills.explanation: Correct: がっかり = disappointed.

drills.sentence: 大事な約束を、うっかりわざと破ってしまった。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: うっかり means carelessly, by accident; it cannot combine with わざと (on purpose).

drills.sentence: 慎重な彼は、よく確かめずにすぐ決めてしまう。
drills.explanation: Incorrect: a 慎重 (careful) person checks before deciding.

choices: treasuring each encounter as if it happens only once
killing two birds with one stone
drills.explanation: From the tea ceremony: each meeting is unique.

choices: failing seven times out of eight
a clumsy person who always trips
a week full of good luck
getting up again every time you fall; never giving up
drills.explanation: Fall seven times, rise eight.

choices: great talents take time to mature
drills.explanation: A great vessel takes long to complete.

choices: forgetting the past to move on
learning new things by studying the old
drills.explanation: Review the old to learn the new.

choices: your deeds come back to you, good or bad
cause and effect cannot be known
drills.explanation: Karmic retribution.

choices: blindly going along with others' opinions
drills.explanation: Echoing others like thunder echoes.
So bad that words fail.

choices: being fooled by a superficial difference
drills.explanation: From the monkeys given three nuts in the morning and four at night.

choices: twisting things to one's own advantage
drills.explanation: Drawing water to your own rice field.

choices: walking a long way in fog
completely lost, not knowing what to do
drills.explanation: In a fog five ri deep.

choices: unprecedented and unlikely ever to be repeated
drills.explanation: Never before, never after.
Calling a needle a pole.
Running east and west on business.
A classic school motto.

choices: worth a thousand others; extraordinarily capable
drills.explanation: One horseman equal to a thousand.

choices: almost the same, with only minor differences
drills.explanation: Largely the same, slightly different.

choices: false advertising; not delivering what is promised
drills.explanation: Showing a sheep's head, selling dog meat.
A thousand differences, ten thousand distinctions.

choices: giving something valuable to someone who can't appreciate it
drills.explanation: Gold coins to a cat.

choices: advice that falls on deaf ears
drills.explanation: A sutra in a horse's ear.

choices: what is done cannot be undone
drills.explanation: Spilled water does not return to the tray.

choices: good advice is often hard to hear
drills.explanation: Good medicine tastes bitter.

choices: those who stand out get criticised
drills.explanation: The protruding stake gets hammered down.

choices: truly able people do not show off
drills.explanation: A clever hawk hides its talons.

drills.word: 井の中の蛙大海を知らず
choices: having a narrow view of the world
staying safe at home is best
drills.explanation: A frog in a well knows nothing of the ocean.
The child of a frog is a frog.
A cane before you fall.

drills.word: 案ずるより産むが易し
choices: things are easier to do than you feared
drills.explanation: Giving birth is easier than worrying about it.

drills.word: 三人寄れば文殊の知恵
choices: two (or three) heads are better than one
too many cooks spoil the broth
drills.explanation: Three ordinary people together have the wisdom of Monju.

choices: sleep is more important than money
drills.explanation: Rising early is worth three mon.

choices: a good brush makes good writing
drills.explanation: Even Kobo Daishi miswrote with his brush.
A rice cake falling from the shelf.
Not knowing, one is at peace like a Buddha.
The mouth is the source of disaster.

drills.word: 好きこそ物の上手なれ
choices: you become good at what you love
drills.explanation: Liking something is how you get good at it.
Regret never comes first.

choices: strike while the iron is hot; act at the right time
drills.explanation: Also: teach people while they are young.
Your face burns red with shame.

choices: to suddenly see things clearly; an eye-opener
drills.explanation: Like scales falling from your eyes.
そわそわする = unable to settle down, e.g. while waiting for results.

scenarios.titleEn: Presenting a report on animal proverbs
scenarios.titleJa: 動物のことわざ調べの発表
scenarios.setting: A sixth-grade Japanese class. You have researched proverbs that contain animals and are presenting your findings to the class. The teacher asks follow-up questions after each part.
scenarios.learnerRole: A sixth-grade student giving a short presentation
scenarios.partnerRole: The homeroom teacher, Ms. Ishida, who asks follow-up questions
goals: Introduce the topic and why you chose it
Explain the meaning of at least two proverbs with an example
Compare two proverbs with similar meanings
Answer the teacher's question and close the presentation politely
phrases: これから発表を始めます。
たとえば、〜ときに使います。
これで発表を終わります。

turns.partnerJa: では、次は木村さんの班ですね。どうぞ始めてください。
turns.partnerEn: Next is Kimura's group. Please go ahead.
turns.intent: Open the presentation and state your topic.
turns.sample: はい。これから、動物が出てくることわざについて発表を始めます。

turns.partnerJa: どうしてそのテーマを選んだんですか。
turns.partnerEn: Why did you choose that theme?
turns.intent: Give your reason for choosing the topic.
turns.sample: 動物が出てくることわざがとても多いことに気づいて、おもしろいと思ったからです。

turns.partnerJa: なるほど。では、一つ目のことわざを紹介してください。
turns.partnerEn: I see. Then please introduce the first proverb.
turns.intent: Explain 猿も木から落ちる and give an example situation.
turns.sample: 一つ目は「猿も木から落ちる」です。上手な人でも失敗することがあるという意味です。たとえば、料理が得意な人が塩と砂糖をまちがえたときに使います。

turns.partnerJa: わかりやすい例ですね。二つ目は何ですか。
turns.partnerEn: That's a clear example. What's the second one?
turns.intent: Explain 猫に小判.
turns.sample: 二つ目は「猫に小判」です。価値がわからない人に大切なものをあげても、役に立たないという意味です。

turns.partnerJa: それと似た意味のことわざを、ほかに見つけましたか。
turns.partnerEn: Did you find any other proverb with a similar meaning?
turns.intent: Compare 猫に小判 with 豚に真珠.
turns.sample: はい、「豚に真珠」です。「猫に小判」と意味がよく似ていますが、こちらは真珠が出てきます。

turns.partnerJa: よく調べましたね。最後に、この調べ学習で気づいたことを教えてください。
turns.partnerEn: Well researched. Lastly, tell us what you noticed through this research.
turns.intent: State your conclusion and close the presentation.
turns.sample: 結論として、ことわざには昔の人の知恵がつまっているとわかりました。これで発表を終わります。ありがとうございました。

scenarios.setting: Your group of four must make a wall newspaper about your town's history by next Friday. You and a classmate are the first to meet after school to divide the work.
scenarios.learnerRole: A fifth-grade student in the group
scenarios.partnerRole: A classmate, Haruto, who is a bit worried about the deadline
goals: Suggest how to divide the roles
Agree on a deadline for each part
Offer to take a task yourself
Encourage your classmate using an idiom
phrases: ぼく（わたし）が〜をやるよ。
みんなで協力すれば大丈夫だよ。

turns.partnerJa: 締め切りまであと一週間しかないよ。間に合うかなあ。
turns.partnerEn: There's only a week left until the deadline. Will we make it?
turns.intent: Reassure him and suggest dividing the work.
turns.sample: 大丈夫だよ。まず役割分担を決めよう。

turns.partnerJa: そうだね。何を分担すればいい？
turns.partnerEn: Right. What should we divide up?
turns.intent: List the tasks: research, writing, drawing, layout.
turns.sample: 資料を調べる人、記事を書く人、絵をかく人、レイアウトを考える人に分けたらどうかな。

turns.partnerJa: ぼくは絵が得意だから、絵を担当しようか。
turns.partnerEn: I'm good at drawing, so shall I do the pictures?
turns.intent: Agree and choose a task for yourself.
turns.sample: いいね。じゃあ、わたしは図書館で資料を調べるよ。

turns.partnerJa: 記事はだれが書く？さくらさんとゆうきくんはまだ来てないけど。
turns.partnerEn: Who'll write the articles? Sakura and Yuki aren't here yet.
turns.intent: Propose giving the articles to the absent members and checking with them.
turns.sample: 二人に記事をお願いしよう。明日、わたしから聞いてみるね。

turns.partnerJa: それぞれ、いつまでに終わらせる？
turns.partnerEn: By when should each of us finish?
turns.intent: Set intermediate deadlines.
turns.sample: 資料と絵は水曜日までに、記事は木曜日までに終わらせよう。金曜日にみんなで貼ろう。

turns.partnerJa: でも、ほかの宿題もあって、もう猫の手も借りたいよ。
turns.partnerEn: But I have other homework too; I'm swamped.
turns.intent: Sympathise and offer help if he falls behind.
turns.sample: わかるよ。もし絵が間に合わなかったら、わたしも手伝うよ。

turns.partnerJa: ありがとう。なんだかできそうな気がしてきた。
turns.partnerEn: Thanks. I'm starting to feel we can do it.
turns.intent: Encourage him and wrap up.
turns.sample: みんなで協力すれば、きっといい新聞になるよ。がんばろう！

scenarios.titleEn: Class meeting: choosing the class event
scenarios.titleJa: 学級会：お楽しみ会の出し物を決める
scenarios.setting: A 学級会 (class meeting) run by the students. The agenda is deciding what the class will do at the end-of-term party. The class chair calls on you to give and defend an opinion.
scenarios.learnerRole: A sixth-grade student speaking at the class meeting
scenarios.partnerRole: The class chair (議長), a classmate who runs the meeting formally
goals: State your proposal clearly with a reason
Respond to an opposing opinion respectfully
phrases: わたしは〜に賛成です。理由は〜からです。
〜という意見もわかりますが、〜。
多数決で決めるのがいいと思います。

turns.partnerJa: これから学級会を始めます。今日の議題は、お楽しみ会の出し物です。意見のある人は手を挙げてください。
turns.partnerEn: We'll now begin the class meeting. Today's topic is what to do at the class party. Raise your hand if you have an opinion.
turns.intent: Raise your hand and propose a class play.
turns.sample: はい。わたしは、クラス全員で劇をすることを提案します。

turns.partnerJa: 理由を教えてください。
turns.partnerEn: Please give your reason.
turns.intent: Give a reason for the play.
turns.sample: 劇なら全員に役割があって、みんなで協力できるからです。

turns.partnerJa: 今の提案に対して、「練習の時間が足りない」という反対意見が出ています。どう思いますか。
turns.partnerEn: There's an opposing opinion that there isn't enough time to rehearse. What do you think?
turns.intent: Acknowledge the concern and answer it.
turns.sample: その意見もわかります。でも、短い劇にすれば、二週間で十分練習できると思います。

turns.partnerJa: ほかに、クイズ大会がいいという意見もあります。
turns.partnerEn: There's also an opinion in favour of a quiz tournament.
turns.intent: Show respect for different opinions using 十人十色 and suggest combining ideas.
turns.sample: 好きなことは十人十色なので、劇の中にクイズを入れてはどうでしょうか。

turns.partnerJa: おもしろい案ですね。ほかの人の賛否も聞いてみます。…賛成の人が多いようです。
turns.partnerEn: Interesting idea. Let me hear the others' views... It seems many are in favour.
turns.intent: Thank the class and ask how to decide formally.
turns.sample: ありがとうございます。最後は多数決で決めるのがいいと思います。

turns.partnerJa: わかりました。では、多数決をとります。「劇とクイズ」に賛成の人は手を挙げてください。
turns.partnerEn: Understood. We'll take a vote. Those in favour of 'play and quiz', raise your hands.
turns.intent: Vote and say you will accept the result.
turns.sample: はい、賛成です。どちらに決まっても、みんなで協力したいです。

turns.partnerJa: 賛成多数で、「劇とクイズ」に決まりました。脚本を書く係を決めたいのですが。
turns.partnerEn: By majority, 'play and quiz' is decided. We need to choose who writes the script.
turns.intent: Volunteer for the script and suggest a partner.
turns.sample: わたしが脚本を担当します。クイズの部分は、クイズが得意な山田さんと一緒に考えたいです。

turns.partnerJa: ありがとうございます。これで今日の学級会を終わります。
turns.partnerEn: Thank you. This concludes today's class meeting.
turns.intent: Close politely.
turns.sample: ありがとうございました。

scenarios.titleEn: Explaining a proverb to a younger sibling
scenarios.titleJa: 弟にことわざを教える
scenarios.setting: At home after school. Your little brother in second grade has homework asking what a proverb means and doesn't understand it. You explain it simply with an example from everyday life.
scenarios.partnerRole: A younger brother, Sota, in second grade, who asks lots of questions
goals: Explain the meaning of 急がば回れ in simple words

turns.partnerJa: ねえ、「急がば回れ」ってどういう意味？宿題に出てるんだけど。
turns.partnerEn: Hey, what does 'isogaba maware' mean? It's in my homework.
turns.intent: Explain the meaning simply.
turns.sample: 急いでいるときほど、安全な道を行ったほうが早く着くっていう意味だよ。

turns.partnerJa: え？回ったら遅くなるんじゃないの？
turns.partnerEn: Huh? Won't going around make you slower?
turns.intent: Give an everyday example.
turns.sample: たとえばね、近道の公園が工事中だったら、無理に通るとかえって時間がかかるでしょ？

turns.partnerJa: あ、そっか。じゃあ、あわてて宿題をやって、まちがえて全部やり直すのも同じ？
turns.partnerEn: Oh, I see. So rushing my homework, making mistakes and redoing everything is the same?
turns.intent: Confirm and praise his example.
turns.sample: そうそう、それも「急がば回れ」だよ。いい例だね。

turns.partnerJa: じゃあ、ノートに「急がないで、ていねいにやるほうが早い」って書けばいい？
turns.partnerEn: So should I write 'doing it carefully without rushing is faster'?
turns.intent: Approve and encourage him.
turns.sample: うん、それでいいよ。よくわかったね。じゃあ、ていねいに書いてね。

turns.partnerJa: ありがとう、お兄ちゃん！ほかのことわざも教えてね。
turns.partnerEn: Thanks! Teach me other proverbs too.
turns.intent: Promise to teach another one later.
turns.sample: いいよ。宿題が終わったら、「猿も木から落ちる」も教えてあげる。

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 大輝くん、リコーダーの練習、がんばってるね。
lines.en: Daiki, you're working hard at your recorder practice.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: でも先生、この曲、何回やっても指が動かないんです。
lines.en: But Miss, however many times I try this piece, my fingers won't move.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 最初はみんなそうだよ。上手な人も、一朝一夕にできたわけじゃないの。
lines.en: Everyone's like that at first. Even the good players didn't get there overnight.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: いっちょういっせき？どういう意味ですか。
lines.en: Itchō isseki? What does that mean?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ほんの短い時間、という意味。つまり、こつこつ続けることが大事なのよ。
lines.en: It means a very short time. In other words, keeping at it steadily is what matters.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 石の上にも三年、ってことですね。
lines.en: So it's like 'three years on a stone', right?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そのとおり。毎日十分でいいから、ゆっくり練習してみて。
lines.en: Exactly. Ten minutes a day is fine; try practising slowly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: わかりました。発表会までに、一生懸命練習します！
lines.en: Got it. I'll practise with all my might before the recital!

questions.question: What does the teacher advise Daiki to do?
choices: Practise a little every day, slowly
Practise for three hours a day

questions.question: Which proverb does Daiki use to show he understood?

dialogues.title: Too busy before the school festival

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 健太、看板の色ぬり、まだ終わってないの？
lines.en: Kenta, haven't you finished painting the sign yet?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ごめん。飾りも作らなきゃいけないし、猫の手も借りたいよ。
lines.en: Sorry. I have to make the decorations too; I'm so busy I'd take help from anyone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: しかたないなあ。わたしが手を貸すよ。
lines.en: Oh well. I'll give you a hand.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 助かる！でも、弟の翔も手伝いに来るって言ってて…。
lines.en: That's a lifesaver! But my little brother Sho says he's coming to help too...

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 翔くん？いたずら好きだから、先生もよく手を焼くって言ってたよね。
lines.en: Sho? He loves pranks; the teachers say they often have a hard time with him.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そうなんだよ。ペンキで遊ばないように、釘を刺しておくよ。
lines.en: Exactly. I'll warn him in advance not to play with the paint.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: それがいいね。じゃあ、わたしは看板、健太は飾りを担当しよう。
lines.en: Good idea. Then I'll do the sign and you do the decorations.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 了解。これで間に合いそうだ。ありがとう、美咲。
lines.en: Got it. Looks like we'll make it now. Thanks, Misaki.

questions.question: Why is Kenta behind with his work?
choices: He has two jobs to do: the sign and the decorations

questions.question: What will Kenta do about his little brother?
choices: Ask the teacher to watch him
Warn him beforehand not to play with the paint

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: あかりさん、作文に目を通したよ。夏休みの思い出、楽しく読めた。
lines.en: Akari, I've looked over your composition. I enjoyed reading about your summer memories.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。でも、なんだか読みにくい気がして…。
lines.en: Thank you. But somehow I feel it's hard to read...

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 書きたいことがたくさんあって、順番がばらばらなんだ。起承転結を意識してみたらどうかな。
lines.en: You have lots you want to say, and the order is jumbled. How about keeping introduction-development-twist-conclusion in mind?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 「転」の部分には、何を書けばいいんですか。
lines.en: What should I write in the 'twist' part?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: キャンプで道に迷った話があったね。あそこが一番はらはらする場面だから、「転」にぴったりだよ。
lines.en: There was the story about getting lost at camp. That's the most nerve-racking scene, so it's perfect for the 'twist'.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: なるほど！最後は、家族のありがたさに気づいたことでまとめます。
lines.en: I see! I'll wrap up at the end with how I realised how precious my family is.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: いいね。取捨選択して、大事な場面だけを残すともっとよくなるよ。
lines.en: Good. If you select and keep only the important scenes, it'll get even better.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい、書き直してみます。
lines.en: Okay, I'll try rewriting it.

questions.question: What is the main problem with Akari's composition?
choices: The order of events is jumbled
It is about the wrong topic

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ぼくがバトンを落とさなければ、一位になれたのに…。
lines.en: If I hadn't dropped the baton, we could have come first...

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そんなに肩を落とさないでよ。みんな蓮のことを責めてないよ。
lines.en: Don't be so downhearted. Nobody's blaming you, Ren.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: でも、アンカーの拓也にも悪いことをしたし、耳が痛い話だけど、練習不足だったと思う。
lines.en: But I let Takuya, our anchor, down too. It's painful to admit, but I think I didn't practise enough.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 拓也も「もう水に流そう」って言ってたよ。
lines.en: Takuya was saying 'Let's forget about it' too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 本当？それなら、来年こそバトンパスの腕を磨くよ。
lines.en: Really? Then next year I'll definitely polish my baton-passing skills.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: その意気だよ。七転び八起き、だね。
lines.en: That's the spirit. Fall seven times, get up eight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: うん。くよくよしてないで、明日から朝練だ！
lines.en: Yeah. No more moping; morning practice starts tomorrow!

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: わたしも一緒に走ってあげる。
lines.en: I'll run with you.

questions.question: Why did the class not win the relay?
What does Ren decide to do?
